notes.note: Nintendo Switch Pro and compatible aftermarket controllers are now supported on Windows and map correctly in web games.
Firefox now opens mailto: links only in response to an explicit user action, so pages can no longer launch the default mail client unprompted.
Small PDFs can now be enlarged when printing by setting the scale above 100%, up to the size of the sheet of paper.
Starting with Firefox 154, Firefox Nightly now supports the `alpha()` CSS function. This is a relative color function that can be used to modify just the alpha component of a given color.

Starting with Firefox 153, Firefox Nightly ships an [experimental implementation][1] of the `link-parameters` property by Tyler Thrailkill.


  [1]: https://drafts.csswg.org/css-link-params-1/
Starting with Firefox 153, Firefox Nightly now supports two new keywords, `closest-corner` and `farthest-corner`, for the radial size in the `circle()` and `ellipse()` functions.

Starting with Firefox 154, Firefox Nightly now supports QUIC version 2 ([RFC 9369][1]) for HTTP/3 connections. Firefox offers both QUIC v1 and v2 using compatible version negotiation ([RFC 9368][2]). The server selects which version is used, so connections upgrade to QUIC v2 when the server chooses it and remain on QUIC v1 otherwise.




  [1]: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9369
  [2]: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9368

Firefox now supports the [`progress()`][1] CSS function. This is a math function that can be used in calculations to compute the position of a value relative to a start and an end.


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Values/progress

SVG `<a>` elements now expose the same [URL properties][1] as HTML links, including `protocol`, `host`, `pathname`, and `search`.


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/HTMLAnchorElement#instance_properties
Starting with Firefox 155, the RegExp Buffer Boundary proposal is now available for testing in Nightly builds by setting the `javascript.options.experimental.regexp_buffer_boundaries` preference.
The CSS Typed Object Model's `StylePropertyMap` now supports `delete()` for removing a property.

Starting with Firefox 155, Firefox Nightly offers limited support for the [Speculation Rules API][1] for same-origin prefetch, allowing pages to declare which links should be prefetched. This initial support covers only the `immediate` eagerness level and `list` source rules.
[1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Speculation_Rules_API

The CSS [`attr()`][1] function now supports values of any type, so authors can use attribute values in any property rather than only as strings in the `content` property.


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Values/attr

The emulation options have moved into a new emulation panel, available behind the @ button in the Rules View, which also offers new toggles to emulate the [`prefers-reduced-motion`][1] media feature.


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/At-rules/@media/prefers-reduced-motion
The JSON Viewer now displays JSON Lines (JSONL/NDJSON) documents, including inline errors for invalid lines.
Fixed Firefox preventing Linux systems from going to sleep after a long browsing session.
Fixed arrow-key and Page Up/Down scrolling not working on some pages with embedded content from other sites.
Fixed characters from some less common scripts appearing as empty boxes on Windows.
Fixed text disappearing in Microsoft 365 Word Online on Linux when typing accented or non-Latin characters with certain keyboard layouts.

On [Firefox for Android][1], autofill prompts now dismiss when focus moves away instead of remaining open until back navigation.


  [1]: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.mozilla.fenix

Starting with Firefox 154, we're testing a simpler tab context menu in Firefox Labs. It can be turned on in *Settings > Firefox Labs > Streamline tab menu*, and feedback is welcome on [Mozilla Connect][1].


  [1]: https://connect.mozilla.org/t5/discussions/try-streamlined-tab-menu-in-nightly-firefox-labs-154/td-p/131285

## Windows

### Operating Systems (32-bit and 64-bit)
 - Windows 10 or later

### Recommended Hardware
-  1 gigahertz (GHz) or faster compatible processor or System on a Chip (SoC)
-  1GB of RAM / 2GB of RAM for the 64-bit version
-  500MB of hard drive space

---

## Mac

### Operating Systems
- macOS 10.15 or later

### Recommended Hardware
- Macintosh computer with an Intel x86 or Apple silicon processor
- 512 MB of RAM
- 200 MB hard drive space

---

## GNU/Linux

### Software Requirements

*Please note that GNU/Linux distributors may provide packages for your distribution which have different requirements.*

- Firefox will not run at all without the following libraries or packages:
    - glibc 2.17 or higher (2.28 or higher on arm64)
    - GTK+ 3.14 or higher
    - libglib 2.42 or higher
    - libstdc++ 4.8.1 or higher (6.0 or higher on arm64)
    - X.Org 1.0 or higher (1.7 or higher is recommended)
- For optimal functionality, we recommend the following libraries or packages:
    - DBus 1.0 or higher
    - NetworkManager 0.7 or higher
    - PulseAudio

Firefox Nightly gets updated every day and as a consequence, the release notes for the Nightly channel are updated continuously to reflect features that have reached sufficient maturity to benefit from community feedback and bug reports. 

**Warning: Features listed here may or may *not* make a final release of Firefox.**

In addition to these release notes, you can follow ongoing development on our [@FirefoxNightly][1] Bluesky account, our [@FirefoxNightly][4] Mastodon account as well as read our [Nightly Blog][2].

You can interact with other Firefox Nightly users and give your feedback to Mozilla staff in the [Nightly Matrix room][3] on chat.mozilla.org.


  [1]: https://bsky.app/profile/firefoxnightly.bsky.social
  [2]: https://blog.nightly.mozilla.org
  [3]: https://chat.mozilla.org/?#/room/#nightly:mozilla.org
  [4]: https://mastodon.social/@FirefoxNightly
